words: مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan tells Adam and Eve that God prohibited eating the tree so they would not become angels or immortals.
rows.anchor: ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits لا, understood from context, as in 4:176, where the sense is that God explains so people will not go astray.
rows.anchor: كما أسقطت من قوله:

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
rows.claim: A Basran grammarian takes the exception as expressing aversion: God forbade the tree because He disliked their becoming angels, by analogy with a warning given out of fear of an outcome.
rows.anchor: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يزعم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ويحيى بن أبي كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Yaḥyā b. Abī Kathīr are reported to read malikayn with kasra, meaning two kings; they connect this interpretation to the imperishable dominion of 20:120.
rows.anchor: وكأن ابن عباس ويحيى وجها تأويل الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī insists on the widely transmitted regional reading with fatḥa, meaning two angels, and says no other reading is permissible.
rows.anchor: القراءة التي عليها قراء الأمصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immortals are those who remain in Paradise forever and do not die.
rows.anchor: أو تكونا من الخالدين في الجنة الماكثين فيها أبدا فلا تموتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed Shuʿayb’s deniers and left their town empty, as if they had never settled or lived there.
rows.anchor: يقال: غني فلان بمكان كذا فهو يغنى به غنى وغنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ghaniya bi-makān means to dwell or be in a place; the anonymous verse using yaghni and Ruʾba’s maghnā illustrate the usage and derivation.
rows.anchor: وعهد مغنى دمنة بضلفعا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as if they had never lived there or enjoyed life there.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يعيشوا، كأن لم ينعموا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that they seemed never to have lived there.
rows.anchor: يقول: كأن لم يعيشوا فيها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the phrase as if they had never been there at all.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يكونوا فيها قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb’s followers were not the losers; God refuted the deniers’ warning in 7:90 by making the deniers the ones destroyed when punishment came.
rows.anchor: شعيبا قالوا للذين أرادوا اتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dispersed the Children of Israel through the lands as separate groups.
rows.anchor: وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that every land entered by a people had a group of Jews in it.
rows.anchor: في كل أرض يدخلها قوم من اليهود

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the dispersed groups as Jews.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the Israelites, some were righteous, meaning believers in God and His messengers, while others fell below that standard.
rows.anchor: من يؤمن بالله ورسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This description applied before they turned back from their religion and disbelieved, before Jesus son of Mary was sent among them.
rows.anchor: قبل ارتدادهم عن دينهم وقبل كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good things are prosperity, comfort, ease, and abundance of provision; the bad things are hardship, austere living, calamities, and losses of wealth.
rows.anchor: وهي الحسنات التي ذكرها جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested them so that they would return to obedience, turn back to Him, and repent of their sins.
rows.anchor: وينيبوا إليها، ويتوبوا من معاصيه

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing idol worshippers, al-Ṭabarī says the idols they call and worship as gods are servants owned by their Lord, just as humans are His servants; worshipping them is associating partners and disbelief.
rows.anchor: يقول: هم أملاك لربكم، كما أنتم له مماليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If idols cannot hear a caller and answer, they cannot harm or benefit; only one who hears requests and can reward, punish, or help can truly bring benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: سمع مسألة سائل وأعطى وأفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions test whether idols can travel to help worshippers, defend and support them, see what is hidden from them, or hear and report what they cannot hear.
rows.anchor: في حوائجكم ويتصرفون بها في منافعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument is that people revere what they expect to provide benefits through such faculties, so worship of images lacking all these means of gaining benefit or avoiding harm makes no sense.
rows.anchor: والمعظم من الأشياء إنما يعظم لما يرجى منه من المنافع التي توصل إليه بعض هذه المعاني عندكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command to plot, the addressed plural includes the idolaters and their idols.
rows.anchor: أنتم وهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge means do not delay your plotting or trickery; act at once.
rows.anchor: يقول: فلا تؤخرون بالكيد والمكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge shows that God protected the Prophet from them and that their idols cannot defend worshippers who seek to harm him.
rows.anchor: ويعرف الكفرة به عجز أوثانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī admonishes the listener not to disdain worship and identifies humble reverence as worship.
rows.anchor: عن التواضع له والتخشع، وذلك هو العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels near God do not disdain submission and humble reverence to Him; this humility is worship.
rows.anchor: عن التواضع له والتخشع، وذلك هو العبادة

words: إِن يَنتَهُوا۟ يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Meccan polytheists stop their unbelief and fighting God, His Messenger, and believers, and repent into faith, their prior sins are forgiven through faith and repentance.
rows.anchor: إن ينتهوا عما هم عليه مقيمون من كفرهم بالله ورسوله وقتالك وقتال المؤمنين فينيبوا إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they resume fighting after Badr, God will punish them as He punished earlier peoples who rebelled, denied messengers, and rejected their counsel.
rows.anchor: فقد مضت سنتي في الأولين منهم ببدر ومن غيرهم من القرون الخالية إذ طغوا وكذبوا رسلي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the precedent concerns Quraysh at Badr and other nations before them.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {فقد مضت سنة الأولين}

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq interprets their return as returning to war against the Prophet and says the earlier precedent is their people killed at Badr.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال في قوله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says that if they return to fight, the precedent is that of the people of Badr.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: «وإن يعودوا لقتالك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says there was no emigration after the conquest, only martyrdom thereafter, and describes believers in three categories; emigrants and the Helpers formed the two allied groups.
rows.anchor: لا هجرة بعد الفتح، إنما هو الشهادة بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s account, emigrants and Helpers who sheltered and supported them were allies and inherited from one another through religious allegiance; believers who did not emigrate did not inherit because they had neither emigrated nor supported the community.
rows.anchor: ورثه الأنصاري بالولاية في الدين

words: وَإِنِ ٱسْتَنصَرُوكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ فَعَلَيْكُمُ ٱلنَّصْرُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Helpers had to aid those appealing for help in religion, except against a people bound to the Prophet by treaty; help was due against enemies without a covenant.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يستنصروا على قوم بينهم وبين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ميثاق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God later gave each believing relative an assigned inheritance share, attaching emigrants and non-emigrants to their kin.
rows.anchor: ثم أنزل الله بعد ذلك أن ألحق كل ذي رحم برحمه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the final three verses of al-Anfāl describe the earlier inheritance-based allegiance between Muslim emigrants and Helpers, which was then abrogated by the final verse on kinship.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " الثلاث الآيات خواتيم الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers are one another’s supporters and allies, with stronger claim to one another than believers have to them; al-Ṭabarī notes an earlier view that this concerned inheritance between them.
rows.anchor: يقول: بعضهم أعوان بعض وأنصاره، وأحق به من المؤمنين بالله ورسوله

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abū Mālik reports that the verse came after a man said they should inherit from their polytheist relatives.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك، قال: " قال رجل: نورث أرحامنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed concerning inheritance from polytheists under treaty.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {والذين

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says emigrant and non-emigrant believers, even brothers, initially did not inherit from one another; after the conquest ended emigration, kin inherited across locations, as in 8:75, and the Prophet said there is no emigration after the conquest.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view takes the verse to mean that unbelievers support one another and that a believer who remained in the land of war without emigrating was not truly a believer.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: إن الكفار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the verse condemned people who positioned themselves to join whichever side prevailed; God forbade such equivocation, requiring separation between Muslim and polytheist camps except for a protected treaty payer.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {والذين كفروا بعضهم أولياء بعض}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Helpers sheltered the Prophet and emigrants and supported them and God’s religion; these are true believers, unlike those who stayed among polytheists without emigrating or fighting the Muslims’ enemy.
rows.anchor: معه ونصروهم ونصروا دين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness means God covers their sins by pardoning them.
rows.anchor: لهم ستر من الله على ذنوبهم بعفوه لهم عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their generous provision in Paradise is pleasant food and drink that does not become waste in their bodies, but exits as sweat like musk.
rows.anchor: لا يتغير في أجوافهم فيصير نجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise and reward in 8:74 show that guardianship in 8:72 means support and aid, not inheritance: if inheritance were intended, the following verse would urge its continuation. Thus these verses contain no abrogating or abrogated ruling.
rows.anchor: إنما هو النصرة والمعونة دون الميراث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrite men and women profess faith to believers with their tongues while concealing disbelief in God and His Messenger; they are one class and share this pattern.
rows.anchor: في إعلانهم الإيمان واستبطانهم الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their command to evil means urging one another to disbelieve in God and Muhammad, reject the revelation, and deny it.
rows.anchor: وهو الكفر بالله وبمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They discourage faith in God, His Messenger, and the revelation brought from God.
rows.anchor: وينهونهم عن الإيمان بالله ورسوله وبما جاءهم به من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They withhold spending for God and charity, denying the people entitled to it the zakat God required from their wealth.
rows.anchor: ويمسكون أيديهم عن النفقة في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses their clasped hands as not opening them to spend for what is right.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {ويقبضون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they do not open their hands to do good, withholding every good act.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {ويقبضون أيديهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They abandoned obedience to God and following His commands, so God left them without His guidance, direction, or mercy.
rows.anchor: نسوا من الخير، ولم ينسوا من الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, as established earlier with supporting examples, forgetting means abandoning or leaving something.
rows.anchor: نسوا من الخير، ولم ينسوا من الشر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they forgot what is good, but did not forget what is evil.
rows.anchor: نسوا من الخير، ولم ينسوا من الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites feign faith to believers while concealing disbelief, and thus depart from obedience and from belief in God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: هم المفارقون طاعة الله الخارجون عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing men and women are those who affirm God, His Messenger, and the signs of His Book; they support and help one another.
rows.anchor: فإن صفتهم أن بعضهم أنصار بعض وأعوانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining right means urging people to believe in God, His Messenger, and the revelation He sent.
rows.anchor: يأمرون الناس بالإيمان بالله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They perform the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: يؤدون الصلاة المفروضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They give the obligatory zakat to those entitled to receive it.
rows.anchor: ويعطون الزكاة المفروضة أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They obey God and His Messenger by carrying out their commands and avoiding what they forbid.
rows.anchor: فيأتمرون لأمر الله ورسوله وينتهون عما نهيناهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will rescue people with these qualities from punishment and admit them to Paradise, unlike hypocrites who command evil and withhold God’s due.
rows.anchor: فينقذهم من عذابه ويدخلهم جنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty in punishing the disobedient, with no one able to prevent or defend against Him, and wise in all His actions and punishments.
rows.anchor: لا يمنعه من الانتقام منه مانع ولا ينصره

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says that throughout the Quran, enjoining right means calling people from associating partners to Islam, while forbidding wrong means forbidding worship of idols and devils.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية، قال: " كل ما ذكره الله في القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the prayer as the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {يقيمون الصلاة} [التوبة: 71] قال: الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite pledges that if God gives him wealth and expands his provision, he will give charity and act righteously by maintaining kinship and spending in God’s cause.
rows.anchor: لئن أعطانا الله من فضله

words: فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَىٰهُم مِّن فَضْلِهِۦ بَخِلُوا۟ بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once God gave them wealth, they withheld charity, refused to maintain relatives, and did not spend for God; they turned away from their covenant.
rows.anchor: بفضل الله الذي آتاهم فلم يصدقوا منه ولم يصلوا منه قرابة ولم ينفقوا منه في حق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turning away and being averse refers to turning away from the covenant they had made with God.
rows.anchor: وأدبروا عن عهدهم الذي عاهدوه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hypocrisy resulted from withholding God’s due from His gift, breaking their promise, and violating their covenant; it remained in their hearts until death, and they were deprived of repentance.
rows.anchor: ببخلهم بحق الله الذي فرضه عليهم فيما آتاهم من فضله وإخلافهم الوعد الذي وعدوا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day they meet God means the day they die and leave this world.
rows.anchor: وذلك يوم مماتهم وخروجهم من الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the man as the Anṣārī Thaʿlaba b. Ḥāṭib, who publicly pledged charity, giving each person their due, and maintaining kin; after receiving wealth he broke his promise, angered God, and his story was revealed in these verses.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {ومنهم من عاهد الله
